newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak refiner sees H1 results next week.
newsitem.headline: Slovak refiner sees H1 results next week.

text.p: Audited first half results of Slovak oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. should be released next week, Slovnaft General Director Slavomir Hatina told Reuters in an interview.
Slovnaft officials had said the results would be ready by the end of September. Hatina gave no reason for the delay.
In a preliminary, unaudited report, the firm said in August its pre-tax profit had fallen to 291.4 million crowns from 2.26 billion for the same period in the previous year.
Slovnaft officials said the main reasons for lower profit was maintenance of major production units and an increase of the world prices of crude oil.

From early March to end April, Slovnaft shut 70 percent of its refining capacity due to the maintenance project, which resulted in a gross loss of 132.72 million crowns for the first quarter of this year, compared to pre-tax profit of 907.74 million in first quarter of 1995.
Slovnaft's sales dropped to 14.062 billion crowns in January-June period, from 15.628 billion in the first half in 1995.
An increase in petrol prices of about five percent in Slovakia came later than the growth of the world prices of crude oil, which also contributed to the decline in profit, officials said.
Hatina said production was now back to full capacity and that 1996 production should reach around 5.1 million tonnes, roughly the same as in 1995.
In the first six months of this year Slovnaft processed 2.418 million tonnes of oil, compared to 2.470 million tonnes in the same period last year.
